narr: A passing upper level trough with strong mid-level flow and diurnal heating under a moist low-level airmass helped generate severe storms across the Ohio River Valley. Effective bulk shear was 30-40kts and supported storm organization. ML CAPE ranged from 1000-2000J/kg by mid-afternoon, steep lapse rates helped efficient downdraft acceleration. ||Training storms also created localized flooding along a convergence axis from southeast Ohio to southwest PA.
